architecture.title: Alto Ops Claw — one NAT workflow, three front ends, two kinds of tools
architecture.caption: One YAML file (workflow.laptop.yml) defines the agent: a tool_calling_agent with a Python tool (chiller_kpi, reads the CSV) and an MCP tool group (bms_tools, reads the mock BMS; include: read_point + list_alarms). The same file runs as `nat run` (console), `nat serve` (REST + OpenAI-compatible, :8001) and `nat mcp serve` (tools over MCP, :9901). The LLM is laptop Ollama here (LAPTOP STAND-IN), vLLM :8000 on the Spark, or https://inference.local/v1 inside an OpenShell sandbox. (Research tutorial Part 3; every path and port checked on NAT 1.9.0 in labs 04-1 to 04-5.)

sequence.title: One chiller question through /v1/workflow/full (lab 04-3, LAPTOP STAND-IN)
sequence.caption: Measured on this Mac: two LLM calls and one tool call per question. The plan call took 4.04 s (365 prompt / 154 completion tokens) and asked for chiller_kpi(hours=6); the tool answered in 0.01 s; the summary call took 5.99 s (445 / 256 tokens). The stream carries `data:` answer chunks and `intermediate_data:` steps (filter_steps=LLM_END,TOOL_END). Laptop numbers, never Spark numbers.

steps.label: data: chunks + intermediate_data: LLM_END, TOOL_END, LLM_END

charts.title: Where one answer's time goes (LAPTOP STAND-IN)
charts.caption: Measured by lab 04-3 from /v1/workflow/full steps (event_timestamp − span_event_timestamp) on this Mac with nemotron-3-nano in Ollama. The tool is ~0.1% of the time; the two LLM calls are the rest. Not Spark numbers.

charts.title: Tokens per LLM call for one chiller question (LAPTOP STAND-IN)
charts.caption: usage_info.token_usage from the two LLM_END steps in lab 04-3 (1,220 tokens in total). /v1/chat/completions reported prompt_tokens 0 on NAT 1.9.0, so count tokens from the steps.

charts.title: Wall time per nat serve endpoint (LAPTOP STAND-IN)
charts.caption: One request each, lab 04-3 on this Mac. The chat request is shorter because the vague question got a clarifying reply with no tool call. Laptop Ollama is shared with other labs, so repeat runs vary (lab 04-1 saw 40–70 s under load).

charts.title: Mock BMS tools: on the server vs offered to the agent
charts.caption: Lab 04-4 step B2: the mcp_client group connects to all 4 tools the mock BMS lists; include: [read_point, list_alarms] offers the agent 2. That is agent config, not a boundary — Exercise 04's OpenShell policy (protocol: mcp, deny_rules write_setpoint) is.
